mutations.find:
const shielded = group.filter(q => q.shield), hit = group.filter(q => !q.shield);
      for (const q of shielded) q.shield = false;
mutations.replace:
const shielded = group.filter(q => q.shield && q.owner === 'ai'), hit = group.filter(q => !shielded.includes(q));
      for (const q of group) q.shield = false;
mutations.documentedRule: Shield: any piece entering the cell gets a shield that ignores the next trap it enters (effects never look at ownership).
mutations.intendedViolation: A shielded HUMAN piece that enters an effect cell is NOT protected: the effect fires on it and its shield is silently used up. A shielded AI piece in the same situation is protected (a 'shielded' event, the effect does not apply). Same effect, equivalent conditions, different result by owner.
mutations.whyRefereeDoesNotHideIt: The referee's sandbox trial (E2 symmetry, tier-2 extra scenarios) always enters with a fresh lone piece whose shield is false, so a shielded entry is never simulated by the referee.

mutations.documentedRule: Burn on entry: an effect cell fires once and is used up the first time a piece arrives on it, whether it walked there or was moved there by another effect (unless the chain cap of 4 is reached, in which case it does not fire).
mutations.intendedViolation: When a piece is FORCED onto an effect cell by another effect (chain arrival, e.g. after a shove), the second cell fires but is not used up. It stays live on the board and fires again on a later arrival.
mutations.whyRefereeDoesNotHideIt: The referee's E3 check (each cell fires at most once) only re-enters the newly placed cells by a normal move; it never re-visits a cell that was reached by a forced chain arrival.

mutations.documentedRule: Actions: each turn a player gets one move action per own piece still on the board (+1 only from a haste effect).
mutations.intendedViolation: Every odd-numbered turn gets one extra action. Turn 1 is the first mover's, so the first mover gets +1 action on EVERY one of its turns, the second mover never does.
mutations.whyRefereeDoesNotHideIt: Turn start is not part of the placement referee at all; the trial sets its own action counts.
